observations.title: Google #BuildHybridAI submission details are live, but prize allocation conflicts within the official page
observations.claim: The current official Devpost page gives a November 11, 2026 submission opening at 9:00 AM Pacific and a November 30 close at 2:00 PM Pacific. It now details requirements: all app inference must use Firebase AI Logic hybrid inference; target Web/Chrome, Android or iOS; App Check is required (debug tokens accepted); submissions need a public GitHub/GitLab repository with an open-source license, a working demo, a YouTube video no longer than three minutes, and an app available free of charge. Existing apps are allowed if significantly updated. The page is internally inconsistent about awards: its detailed prize text says $30,000 total including a $10,000 Grand Prize and $3,000 platform awards, while its lower prize section says $30,000 Grand Prize for one winner. The linked Official Rules page still says rules are unavailable. Optional Google Account Quota is discretionary and lasts four days after issuance; the first request window closes November 11 at 2:00 PM Pacific.
observations.why_now: Scheduled recheck on the advertised submission-opening date found the detailed build requirements and a material contradiction in the prize allocation. The earlier journal's claim of a $30,000 one-winner grand prize cannot be treated as settled.
observations.value: Cash prizes are advertised, but the prize allocation is contradictory within the current official page; do not count $30,000 as a verified single-winner award or as accessible funding.
observations.eligibility: Individuals, teams and organizations in most countries may participate if above the legal age of majority and not in excluded jurisdictions. Solo entry is permitted. Existing apps may qualify if significantly updated during the competition. Final official rules remain unavailable.
observations.friction: All app inference must run through Firebase AI Logic; public repository and open-source license required; App Check required; demo video must be public on YouTube and no longer than three minutes; app must be free. Optional advanced-feature quota is approval-gated and lasts only four days. Submission opening is 9:00 AM Pacific November 11; at this check it had not yet opened.
observations.observed_delta: New detailed requirements are now visible. The official page contradicts itself on whether the $30,000 is the total prize pool or the one-winner grand prize; the separate rules page still says unavailable. Preserve the earlier $30,000 claim as unresolved rather than silently correcting history.
observations.anti_leverage: Prize amount and final rules are unresolved; three-week build and public open-source/demo requirements impose real time cost. Do not divert SECONDS MATTER work or assume any quota approval.

observations.title: Voyager free plan provides 1,000 monthly agent credits plus local creative engines and MCP/skills integrations
observations.claim: Voyager's current first-party FAQ and pricing page say every new account receives a free plan with 1,000 workspace credits per month, capped at 500 credits in any five-hour window, with no card and no rollover. Free includes four agent-chat models, up to 25 Nano Banana images and three stock-voice generations per month. One credit equals one cent of provider-priced generation; this is $10-equivalent usage credit, not cash. Voyager says its own Design, Video and DAW engines run locally and are included free with no watermark or project limits. The app supports user-added MCP servers and custom skills, and the same creative skills/CLI tools can be used from Claude Code or Codex. Own provider keys are allowed on Free but are billed by the provider; the user's own Claude or ChatGPT subscription is not billed by Voyager. Project files remain local unless a task sends selected files/context to a model provider.
observations.why_now: The product was previously identified in chat after the owner's link, but was not persisted because the prior daily journal had reached its five-observation limit. Current official FAQ and pricing details have now been checked for the durable ledger.
observations.value: 1,000 monthly credits, approximately $10 of provider-priced generation, plus vendor-described local creative editing engines included free. Credits are not cash, do not roll over, and are limited by a 500-credit/five-hour cap.
observations.eligibility: Public Free plan for new accounts; no payment card required. No approval or account creation has been performed.
observations.friction: Desktop application and local hardware required. Free model usage is limited; video/music/3D and broader model access require paid plans unless using provider keys, which incur direct provider charges. Linux has no computer-control support. Model tasks may send selected project files and context to the connected provider.
observations.observed_delta: First durable repository record of the free plan and its MCP/custom-skill/Claude Code/Codex interoperability. No claim that the free tier or integrations were newly launched today.
observations.anti_leverage: Not a replacement for the cloud-first intelligence engine or production infrastructure. The $10 equivalent is capped, non-rollover usage credit; own API keys are not free and model context may leave the device.

observations.title: Correction: Upwork $1,500 home-services voice-AI listing was posted last week, not November 1
observations.claim: Upwork's indexed public listing currently says the $1,500 fixed-price home-services voice-AI snapshot job was posted 'last week'; the November 1 date belongs to the client's membership date, not a verified posting date. The indexed snapshot shows 20–50 proposals, 16 interviews, five invites sent, and the client last viewed the listing last week. The scope includes a pest-control voice agent, missed-call text-back, lead response under 60 seconds, follow-up, calendar booking and a recovered-revenue report. Its stated kickoff milestone was November 5, demo milestone November 12 and handoff November 20. No hire or payment is shown. Direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403, so the listing details remain provisional.
observations.why_now: Recheck identified a prior metadata error: client membership date had been mistaken for job posting date. The correction materially changes freshness and actionability; retain the same stable ID and preserve the earlier observation.
observations.value: $1,500 advertised fixed-price project if selected and delivered; not a contract, earned revenue or settled payment.
observations.eligibility: Listing requests Top Rated or Expert-Vetted freelancers with two live home-services voice-AI builds, a 30-minute screen share, fluent English and overlap with U.S. Eastern hours. Founder eligibility and portfolio qualifications are not established.
observations.friction: 20–50 proposals and 16 interviews; client last viewed last week; stated kickoff date November 5 has passed. Direct Upwork page retrieval is blocked (HTTP 403); no hire or payment is visible.
observations.observed_delta: Corrects the prior journal's unsupported November 1 posting date. November 1 is the client's member-since date; the indexed job says posted last week. The buyer request remains a one-off agency implementation job with substantial qualification barriers.
observations.anti_leverage: This is an agency hiring a specialist, not a home-service business buying a recurring callback service. The $1,500 is proposed project revenue, not subscription demand; no hire or payment is confirmed.
observations.source_access_note: Upwork search index exposed listing details; direct page retrieval returned 403. Keep needs_review and do not treat the milestone schedule as a confirmed contract.

observations.title: Reject Clockwork $78,400 missed-call loss headline as independent market proof
observations.claim: Clockwork's April 10, 2026 report says it analyzed 1,247 U.S. home-service contractors and 2.4 million calls using Clockwork platform call logs, voluntary third-party call-tracking statements, and direct test calls to 340 businesses. Its $78,400 annual lost-revenue figure is modeled using a 41% booking conversion rate from internal Clockwork booking data and average-ticket estimates, rather than observed recovered payments. Clockwork also markets its own free field-service platform and virtual receptionist. The report is a vendor-authored problem hypothesis, not an independent representative national survey or proof that an individual contractor will recover that amount.
observations.why_now: Compared with the already-recorded Invoca benchmark during this buyer-demand review. The report contains useful disclosed methodology but also a direct vendor interest and a modeled revenue headline that could be misused as a sales claim.
observations.value: No cash, credits or verified savings. The $78,400 figure is a vendor-modelled annual estimate, not realized recovered revenue or a customer commitment.
observations.eligibility: Not an opportunity program. Report sample covers contractors in Clockwork's dataset, voluntary third-party statements and 340 direct test calls; representativeness is not independently established.
observations.friction: Vendor-owned dataset and internal conversion assumptions; no independent audit or controlled causal study shown. Do not generalize the headline to all contractors or use it as a guaranteed ROI claim.
observations.observed_delta: Newly reviewed vendor report adds call-answer and after-hours problem hypotheses, but its headline dollar-loss estimate is modeled from internal conversion data and Census ticket estimates. Rejected as independent proof; retain as a low-confidence vendor signal.
observations.anti_leverage: Do not quote $78,400 as a typical contractor loss or promise a comparable recovery. Use customer-specific call logs and measured outcomes instead.

observations.title: Upwork home-services buyer shows one hire on a $10 GHL voice-agent and missed-call setup request
observations.claim: An Upwork-indexed public listing posted November 5, 2026 asks for a GoHighLevel AI voice agent, 24/7 call answering, phone routing, call recording, voicemail and missed-call text-back, CRM tracking, SMS/email follow-up, appointment booking, call summaries and team alerts. It advertises a $10 fixed-price one-time project. The current indexed activity snapshot shows 20–50 proposals, one hire, zero interviews and the client last viewed the listing five days before the search snapshot. One hire is a contract/hiring outcome indicator, but no funded milestone, payout or settled payment is visible. Direct page retrieval returned HTTP 403.
observations.why_now: New public buyer request closely matches SECONDS MATTER's workflow and, unlike several earlier listings, the indexed activity now displays one hire. Preserve the distinction between a hire indicator and verified payment.
observations.value: $10 advertised fixed-price one-time project; one hire is shown in Upwork's indexed activity, but no actual payment amount, funded milestone or settled payout is verified.
observations.eligibility: Worldwide freelancers; listing requests expert-level GoHighLevel Voice AI, Conversation AI, LC Phone or Twilio and workflow experience. Founder qualifications are not established.
observations.friction: 20–50 proposals, $10 headline budget for broad voice/CRM scope, client last viewed five days ago, and direct page fetch blocked. One hire is shown but the successful scope and payment status are unknown.
observations.observed_delta: New listing with one hire displayed. This is stronger than a bare job post but remains below payment_committed/payment_confirmed because no funded milestone or payout evidence is public in the indexed snapshot.
observations.anti_leverage: The $10 budget is not a viable service-price benchmark for the full scope. It is a one-time contractor project, not proof of recurring end-customer demand or sustainable unit economics.
observations.source_access_note: Upwork indexed listing is public, but direct page retrieval returned 403. Keep needs_review; one hire does not establish a settled payment.
